subject: Chain-of-records extractability and retention query for RFP
messages:
From: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Chain-of-records extractability & retention questions for RFP

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for taking our RFP — a few clarifying questions on audit logs / exportability to include in the formal response: 
1) What retention windows are supported out-of-the-box for hosted logs and audit trails? Can customers configure longer retention per account/tenant?
2) For exportability: can we pull raw audit logs (request/response metadata, timestamps, user ids) filtered by org/tenant and date range? Is export incremental or bulk-only?
3) What formats and manifests are produced on export (CSV/NDJSON/parquet)? Do exports include a cryptographic manifest or signatures to prove non-tampering?
4) Encryption: are exports encrypted in-transit and at-rest? Does Redwood support delivery to our S3 with SSE-KMS using our key?
5) Service commitments: typical turnaround time to deliver an evidence bundle for a 12–24 month window (approx 10–30 TB)?
6) Is there an API for scheduled exports for ongoing compliance playbooks, or do we need to run ad-hoc requests?

If you can answer at a high level, that would help; we may follow up with a technical call.

Thanks,
Peter Lowe
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme Financial
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chain-of-records extractability & retention questions for RFP

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I can pull together a short evidence package and schedule a call with our security engineer if you want deeper detail.

1) Retention windows: Hosted-default is 30 days for fine-grained request logs; we offer configurable retention add-ons (90/365/indefinite) as a paid option. Dedicated and Private deployments can set retention policy per-tenant via config and support long-term archived retention.

2) Exportability: Yes — exports can be filtered by tenant, date range, and route/model. We support both bulk one-off exports and incremental exports (cursor-based) via the Audit Export API.

3) Formats & manifests: Primary exports are NDJSON and Parquet (for analytics). Exports include a signed manifest (SHA256 hashes for each file) and an optional signed ledger (RFC-style timestamping) to support tamper-evidence.

4) Encryption & delivery: All exports are TLS-encrypted in transit. We support S3 delivery with SSE-KMS using customer KMS (cross-account role). Client-side encryption is also supported on Private deployments.

5) Turnaround & throughput: Typical delivery depends on size and SLA. For hosted customers without expedited SLA, we quote 3–5 business days for multi-TB bundles; with enterprise SLAs we can commit faster and do direct S3 streaming. We'll include an estimate for your 10–30 TB window.

6) Scheduling/API: We have an Audit Export API that supports scheduled exports (recurring jobs) and on-demand exports. The API returns a manifest and delivery status.

Attachments: redwood-audit_export_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook), export_schema_samples.csv (sample schema).

Next steps: if you confirm the target retention length and approximate data size, Marissa and I will assemble a detailed throughput estimate and a sample signed-manifest. Would you prefer a technical call Thursday or Friday?

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
From: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acme.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chain-of-records extractability & retention questions for RFP

Rohan — quick clarifications from our side before a call: 
- We need cryptographic chain-of-custody: each export must include file-level hashes and a signed manifest with a timestamp we can independently verify. Do you provide an attestation (signed by Redwood) that the export was produced from the live system state?
- Key management: Does Redwood support HSM-backed wrapping and can we supply the KMS key ARN (cross-account)?
- Redaction: Exports must be configurable to include PII redaction tiers; we will need both unredacted and redacted variants for legal/eDiscovery. Are both supported?
- Scope: the RFP estimates 18 months worth of logs (~20 TB). Can you provide a ballpark for parallel export throughput (MB/s per worker) and an end-to-end ETA if you stream direct to our S3?

Thanks — Audrey
Program Manager, IT Controls
Acme Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Audrey Chen <audrey.chen@acme.com>, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Chain-of-records extractability & retention questions for RFP

Hi Audrey — answering inline below and adding some implementation detail so your Security and Platform teams can evaluate.

1) Attestation & signed manifests
- We produce a signed manifest per export that contains file-level SHA256 hashes plus a manifest signature (ECDSA P-256) generated by our audit key. For high-assurance engagements we can provide a time-stamped attestation (RFC 3161) that references the manifest-id. Sample: redwood-evidence-fingerprint-spec.txt (attached).

2) HSM / KMS support
- Hosted: we support SSE-KMS for S3 deliveries; customers can provide the KMS key ARN and we assume a cross-account role to write objects encrypted with your key. For Private installs you can bring your own HSM and we support key wrapping with customer-managed keys.

3) Redaction variants
- Exports support configurable redaction policies. We can produce both fully unredacted bundles (requires contractual controls) and redacted bundles that mask PII according to configurable templates.

4) Throughput & ETA for ~20 TB
- Typical parallel streaming throughput (enterprise-configured export pipeline): 250–400 MB/s aggregate using 8–16 workers, depending on workload and compression. Ballpark ETA to stream 20 TB to your S3: ~14–24 hours if we run an expedited export with reserved throughput; standard ops may be 24–72 hours including validation and signing. We will include a worksheet with calculations. (See attachment: export_throughput_estimate.xlsx)

5) Additional notes
- Exports include a machine-readable manifest and a human-readable report with a chain-of-custody timeline. We can also provide an HMAC-backed incremental export cursor for ongoing sync.
- For legal hold / eDiscovery we recommend using our Dedicated or Private option to meet stricter retention and control SLAs.

We can prepare a short SOC-ready evidence package and a scoped Statement of Process for procurement. Rohan — if you want, Ben and I will coordinate a 45-minute technical review next week with our Security Engineer and Solutions Architect.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
